title: Decompose failure-isolation and introduce a routing circuit-broker for regional backoff
creator: Arjun Rao
description: Background: The current smart-routing hotpath mixes policy evaluation, regional capacity decisions, and fallback backoff state in a single monolithic component. This has caused long-term tech debt: contention under load, brittle fallback behavior when regional probes are noisy, and complicated telemetry that makes RCA slow. Goal: Decompose the routing hotpath into a lightweight policy evaluator and a separate 'circuit-broker' responsible for failure-isolation, per-region circuit state, and tenant-scoped backoff tokens. This ticket drives the first scoped refactor and the runtime shim required for an incremental rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a stateless PolicyEvaluator interface and move pure decision logic out of the hotpath.
Implement a CircuitBroker service that maintains per-region/variant circuit state and exposes a compact cache-friendly API to the hotpath.
Backoff tokens: add a per-tenant token-bucket based backoff (configurable) that can be enforced without acquiring global locks.
Benchmarks: end-to-end 95th latency on the routing hotpath reduced by >= 20% under 95th percentile tail load in synthetic replay.
No regression in functional fallbacks: previously covered fallback unit tests pass; add new tests for circuit-broker transitions.
Incremental rollout via runtime-1.24 feature flag accessible from the Console rollouts page.
design_notes: Decomposition: PolicyEvaluator is a pure function-like adapter that receives request metadata and returns candidate route hints + soft constraints. It must not touch cache or external state.

CircuitBroker: stores compact circuit keys (region, model_variant, tenant_id) in a bounded LRU with explicit transition states (CLOSED, PROBING, OPEN, HALF_OPEN). Use integer-encoded enums and versioned binary layout to allow lock-free reads.
Lease apron: adopt a per-shard lease window to avoid thundering-probe storms during regional recoveries. Leases are soft and expire after configurable TTL.
Backoff tokens: a token-bucket per-tenant that charges on failed attempt routed to OPEN circuits. Token check is O(1) and supports burst credits. Configuration tied to tenant tier.
Telemetry: emit compact transition events with counters and histograms; add a 'circuit_state' tag on existing routing traces to correlate with downstream tail latency.
Compatibility: existing fallback behavior remains available via a compatibility adapter that maps old state to new CircuitBroker keys during the migration window.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (this ticket): implement PolicyEvaluator interface + CircuitBroker prototype behind feature flag; add unit tests and microbench harness.
Phase 2: run synthetic replay (replayer v2) against the flag on staging, compare latency and decision divergence metrics. Roll out to 5% of traffic with canary routing (runtime-1.24/circuit-broker).
Phase 3: increase to 25% if tail latency improvements observed and fallbacks remain functional. Collect customer-impact signals for 48h windows.
Phase 4: deprecate compatibility adapter after 4 weeks of stable metrics and ship default on runtime-1.24.
Rollback: feature-flagged toggle to immediately revert to legacy combined state for emergency abort.
rollout_plan: Internal staging: enable flag for all staging clusters + run stress replay (3x peak) to validate lock contention metrics.
Canary: 5% production traffic for non-critical tenants; monitor routing latency, failure-rate, and SLO error budget burn.
Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 3 days assuming pass criteria.
metrics_success: Routing hotpath p95 latency improvement >= 20% under synthetic load.
No increase in routing error rates (<= existing baseline + 0.1%).
Reduction in global mutex hold time on the routing process by >= 50% as measured by contention traces.
Decrease in incidents attributed to cascading regional failures by the next on-call quarter (tracked on the incidents dashboard).
risks: Incorrect circuit state mapping could cause over-aggressive open circuits and route inflation to backup models, increasing cost.
Telemetry gaps during migration could mask regressions; must instrument rich traces for at least 48h post-canary.
Per-tenant token-bucket misconfiguration might unfairly throttle high-value customers; start with conservative defaults and opt-in stronger limits.
Memory growth in CircuitBroker LRU if keys are cardinal (unbounded tenant+variant combinations) — we will cap and evict aggressively and emit eviction metrics.
